record.paper_title: Open Problem: Tight Bounds for Kernelized Multi-Armed Bandits with Bernoulli Rewards
record.original_question: In a kernelized Bernoulli bandit with unknown f: X -> [0,1] in an RKHS H_k, ||f||_{H_k} <= B, k(x,x) <= 1, and observations y_t sampled from Ber(f(x_t)), can one define a suitable estimator mu_t(x) of f(x) and prove concentration guarantees for the deviation |f(x) - mu_t(x)| that are tight for Bernoulli observations rather than merely using the fact that Bernoulli rewards are 1/2-subgaussian? More specifically, can such guarantees capture the stronger Bernoulli KL-divergence concentration rates known for unstructured multi-armed bandits while handling the correlations among arms induced by the kernelized setting?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a compact set of arms and let $k:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{X}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a positive-definite kernel with $k(x,x)\le 1$ for all $x\in\mathcal{X}$, with associated reproducing kernel Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_k$. Let $f\in\mathcal{H}_k$ be an unknown function with $f(x)\in[0,1]$ for all $x\in\mathcal{X}$ and $\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_k}\le B$ for a known constant $B>0$. In rounds $t=1,2,\dots$, a learner selects $x_t\in\mathcal{X}$ (possibly depending on the past) and observes $y_t\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(f(x_t))$ independently given the history.

For unstructured ($K$-armed) Bernoulli bandits, the KL-UCB analysis yields concentration on the empirical mean $\hat p$ of an arm with true mean $p$ of the form $\mathbb{P}(N\,d(\hat p,p)\ge \delta)\le e^{-\delta}$, where $d(a,b)=a\log(a/b)+(1-a)\log((1-a)/(1-b))$ is the Bernoulli KL-divergence and $N$ is the number of pulls. By contrast, current kernelized-bandit analyses only exploit the $\tfrac12$-subgaussianity of Bernoulli rewards, yielding bounds of the form $|f(x)-\mu_t(x)|\le \beta_t\,\sigma_t(x)$ with $\beta_t$ depending on the maximum information gain.

Question. Does there exist an estimator $\mu_t(x)$ of $f(x)$ (based on the history $\{(x_s,y_s)\}_{s\le t}$) together with confidence functionals $c_t(x)$ such that, for any $\delta\in(0,1)$, with probability at least $1-\delta$ and simultaneously for all $t\ge 1$ and all $x\in\mathcal{X}$,
$$ d\!\bigl(\mu_t(x),\,f(x)\bigr)\ \le\ c_t(x;\delta), $$
where $c_t(x;\delta)$ recovers, in the limit of independent arms, the Bernoulli KL-rate $\tfrac{\log(1/\delta)+\text{lower-order}}{N_t(x)}$, while remaining valid in the kernelized setting where the estimates at different arms are correlated through $k$? Equivalently, can one obtain a concentration inequality for $|f(x)-\mu_t(x)|$ in the kernelized RKHS Bernoulli model that is tight for Bernoulli observations (capturing the variance $f(x)(1-f(x))$) rather than merely the $\tfrac12$-subgaussian bound, and that can be used to derive regret rates strictly improving on those obtained from subgaussian concentration when $f$ takes values close to $0$ or $1$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was posed in 2024 as an explicit open problem. A 2025 follow-up develops a self-normalized Bernstein-like dimension-free inequality for generalized kernelized bandits (covering exponential-family rewards, including Bernoulli) yielding variance-aware concentration and regret bounds. This represents partial progress (variance-aware Bernstein-type bounds), but it is not clear it attains the full KL-divergence-tight Bernoulli rate of Garivier–Cappé in the kernelized regime. The problem is best regarded as still open, with partial progress via Bernstein-type bounds.

status_evidence.snippet: draws attention to this open problem on tight Bernoulli concentration in kernelized bandits

status_evidence.title: Generalized Kernelized Bandits: A Novel Self-Normalized Bernstein-Like Dimension-Free Inequality and Regret Bounds
status_evidence.snippet: novel self-normalized Bernstein-like dimension-free inequality applicable to a Hilbert space of functions with bounded norm; extends kernelized bandits to exponential family rewards
status_evidence.claim: Provides variance-aware (Bernstein-like) concentration covering Bernoulli rewards in the RKHS setting, constituting partial progress.
